featured_reviews.name: Kinjal Jethwa
featured_reviews.review_text:
World of Palates, just a few seconds from Marine Drive, is truly a hidden gem for vegetarians. Celebrating their 1st anniversary on 11th December, they’re offering a special grand menu along with exciting discounts throughout the week — the perfect time to visit. The ambience is warm, cosy and thoughtfully designed, with comfortable seating for both small gatherings and larger groups. The charming book-filled corners add a unique, aesthetic touch.

We visited during their Sunday brunch, and the spread was delightful — fresh loaf breads, hummus, tacos, vibrant salads and juicy fruits that instantly caught the eye. The mains were equally impressive, featuring creamy mac and cheese, sautéed veggies, paneer lababdar, dal tadka, biryani and noodles. The highlight was definitely the desserts, with their pancakes and waffles stealing the show. A must-visit for anyone who loves global flavours and comforting vegetarian food.

featured_reviews.name: Anita Pemgirikar
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Really Nice Lunch Experience

Good food, calm ambience, and a satisfying afternoon meal.

I tried their lunch buffet recently and had a genuinely good time. The dishes were fresh, flavourful, and comforting, the kind of food you actually enjoy without feeling too heavy. The live waffle and pancake counter was a lovely addition, and everything was made perfectly.

The ambience was another highlight. The place is peaceful, clean, and feels welcoming. They also have a nice variety of books you can pick up and read, which makes the whole experience even more relaxing if you like slow, cosy lunches. The service was polite and everything felt smooth and comfortable.

If you’re around Nariman Point and want a lunch that feels calming and genuinely enjoyable, this spot is definitely worth visiting. 🍽️✨

featured_reviews.name: Rajat Bajaj
featured_reviews.review_text:
After a long and hectic day at work, our group decided to unwind and walked across from our Head Office to Worlds of Palate, a charming pure-vegetarian restaurant located right in the heart of Nariman Point. The place immediately gives a sense of calm — a cosy, tastefully done interior with soothing music and warm lighting that makes it perfect for relaxed conversations.

We ordered a spread that truly showcased the kitchen’s range: Veg Biryani, Pesto and Pesto Pizza, and Spaghetti Aglio Olio Pasta. Every dish arrived freshly prepared, beautifully plated, and perfectly balanced in flavour. The biryani was aromatic and not oily, the pizza had a crisp thin crust with a generous layer of pesto and cheese, and the pasta was cooked al dente with authentic Italian seasoning. It’s evident that the restaurant uses quality ingredients and pays attention to detail.

Service was prompt and courteous, with the staff checking in just at the right times — not intrusive, yet attentive. The portion sizes were satisfying, and prices felt reasonable for the location and ambience.

What stood out most was the peaceful atmosphere, quite unlike the busy office district around it. Worlds of Palate manages to create a small oasis of calm in the middle of Mumbai’s corporate hub — ideal for colleagues looking for a quiet dinner or even a quick team lunch.

Overall, it’s a must-visit vegetarian restaurant in Nariman Point for anyone who appreciates freshness, flavour, and a relaxed dining experience. We left refreshed, content, and sure that we'll return soon.

featured_reviews.review_text: We set out on a magnificent culinary adventure at the newly launched Pali Bhavan at Eros, a true gastronomic treasure that shines bright with its sublime Indian cuisine. The ambiance was very laid back, bathed in a warm glow by colonial decor and softly radiant lights. Our delightful odyssey commenced with Tandoori pomfret, Galouti kebab, Malai chicken tikka, and prawn, each dish a brilliant testament to the chef's innovative genius. The main course showcased their legendary crab Sukkha and Kali Dal, masterfully crafted to exhilarate the senses. The crowning glory was the paan kulfi and chocolate roshogolla, desserts that left us utterly enchanted. The food was truly sublime, with flavors that joyfully danced on the palate and desserts that stole the spotlight, rendering the entire experience profoundly unforgettable.

featured_reviews.name: Aakash
featured_reviews.review_text:
There’s an unmistakable old-world charm here; an almost nostalgic, lived-in elegance that feels refreshingly authentic in a city that often chases the new and shiny.

The ambience is wonderfully understated: warm lighting, vintage touches, wooden furniture that has seen stories, and that classic Bombay colonial-meets-Bandra vibe.

The food is rich, deeply flavoured, cooked with real care. Every dish carries that unmistakable depth; nothing is timid or overly polished. The spicing is confident, the portions generous, and the execution consistent. It’s the kind of meal that lingers in memory long after you’ve left.

Whether it’s a quiet celebration, a catch-up with old friends, or simply craving something soulful, Pali Bhavan delivers exactly what one hopes for in a neighbourhood favourite: character, flavour, and comfort in equal measure.

Highly recommended for those who appreciate substance over spectacle.

featured_reviews.review_text: This is a lovely restaurant with absolutely amazing food. Every dish we had was fantastic - some of the best food we have had whilst in India. Friendly and attentive staff and the restaurant has a lovely atmosphere. Highly recommended for anyone visiting Mumbai

featured_reviews.name: Monis
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stepping into Pali Bhavan is less like walking into a restaurant and more like being welcomed into a world carefully curated for the senses. The moment you cross the threshold, a warm, vibrant energy wraps around you — the kind that hums with quiet excitement and makes you instantly glad you came. The interiors are a masterclass in rustic vintage design: weathered textures, artful nostalgia, and thoughtful details that together create an atmosphere that feels both timeless and distinctly alive.

The food is, simply put, exceptional. Every dish arrives as evidence of a kitchen that takes its craft seriously — where quality is not a checkbox but a standard. The menu reads like a love letter to bold, imaginative cooking: innovative, eye-catching, and refreshingly unhurried in its approach. Dish after dish finds a way to surprise, with flavours that linger long after the last bite and an unmistakable ability to awaken the palate in ways you didn't expect.

Equally deserving of praise is the service. The staff carries a warmth that feels genuine — attentive without being intrusive, welcoming without being performative. They move through the room with ease, and their care for the guest experience is palpable. Dining here never once feels rushed; instead, it unfolds at exactly the right pace for a truly relaxed, enjoyable evening.

"Pali Bhavan doesn't just offer a meal — it offers an experience worthy of returning to. South Mumbai has quietly welcomed a new icon, and those who discover it will find themselves planning their next visit before the first one is even over."

featured_reviews.name: Vimall P Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
A Profoundly Disappointing Culinary Experience

My recent visit to Restaurant Shiv Sagar was, without hyperbole, one of the most profoundly disappointing culinary experiences I have ever endured. This establishment fails catastrophically on every metric that defines a worthwhile restaurant, from the moment you sit down until the moment you thankfully leave. I feel compelled to provide a candid account to ensure fellow diners can make an informed choice and avoid the regret we felt.

The most critical failure lies, undoubtedly, with the food. To simply call it subpar would be a significant understatement; it was, quite frankly, one of the worst meals I have ever consumed. Each dish we ordered was a masterclass in mediocrity, lacking any discernible freshness, flavour, or culinary care. The spices were either absent or jarringly unbalanced, and the overall impression was of food that had been prepared with a sheer lack of interest, tasting bland, pre-made, and carelessly reheated. It was an absolute letdown that formed the core of our negative experience.

This culinary disaster was perfectly complemented by an equally dismal physical environment. The ambiance is best described as poor, with a cramped, cluttered, and uninspiring layout. A significant and frustrating practical issue was the size of the tables. They are inexplicably tiny, making it a genuine struggle to accommodate two plates of food alongside basic essentials like water glasses, condiments, and cutlery. This created a constant, uncomfortable juggling act throughout the meal, completely destroying any possibility of a relaxed dining atmosphere.

To complete this trifecta of failure, the service was exceptionally poor. The staff were inattentive, disinterested, and painfully slow. We waited an eternity to place our order, another eternity for the food to arrive, and a final eternity to receive the bill and settle the payment. Simple requests, like a refill of water, were met with indifference and long delays. The complete absence of basic hospitality was the final straw. In conclusion, Restaurant Shiv Sagar offers no compelling reason for a visit. I cannot recommend it and will unequivocally not be returning.

featured_reviews.review_text:

Whether you're in the mood for North Indian, South Indian, or Chinese cuisine, Shiv Sagar delivers delicious options that cater to a variety of tastes.

The restaurant's location is also a major plus. Situated in a prime area, it's easily accessible and adds to the overall convenience of dining here. This makes it an ideal spot for both casual meals and special occasions.

In terms of value for money, Shiv Sagar offers a satisfying experience. The prices are reasonable, especially considering the generous portions and the quality of the ingredients used. This ensures that you get the most out of your dining experience without breaking the bank.

One of the standout features of Shiv Sagar is its nice variety of dishes. The extensive menu ensures that there is something for everyone, from classic favorites to more unique and innovative creations. This variety keeps the dining experience exciting and caters to diverse palates.

Finally, the great service at Shiv Sagar truly enhances the overall experience. The staff is attentive, courteous, and efficient, ensuring that your needs are well taken care of. Their warm hospitality adds a personal touch that makes you feel valued and welcomed.

In summary, Shiv Sagar is a restaurant that offers a winning combination of good quality food, a convenient location, excellent value for money, a diverse menu, and outstanding service. It's a place where you can enjoy a memorable meal with family and friends.

featured_reviews.name: Nomnomnoted
featured_reviews.review_text:
Flavor-Filled Family Spot: A Must-Try for All

This restaurant’s menu is packed with flavor—whether you’re diving into their sandwiches or sipping on their floats, you’re in for a treat. Impressively, their Jain options are just as commendable, making this place a hit for everyone. Portion sizes are generous, so be warned: the jacket potatoes (served with gravy!) and the sizzler are huge. Unless you’re absolutely starving, you might want to go easy on the ordering.
Recommended dishes : Sichuan Marbles, Hummus Platter (even jain was excellent)
The shooters here are basically fun-flavored sodas, guaranteed to entertain the kids. Every dish packs adequate flavor and seasoning, and I’d give them all a solid 4/5. The only letdown was the mac and cheese, but everything else was fantastic. After my meal, I needed a walk—that’s how filling it all was! Rameshwaram Cafe has been on my list for a while, though I walked in with some hesitation given the mixed reviews online. Glad to say, the experience leaned positive.

We ordered the Benne Pudi Masala Dosa, Benne Masala Dosa, Ghee Pudi Idli, and the Filter Coffee Softy. The dosas arrived crisp, generously buttered, and well-balanced in flavour, while the Ghee Pudi Idli stood out for its richness and depth. The Filter Coffee Softy was an interesting, indulgent twist—worth trying for something different.

What works here is consistency in taste and a certain indulgent South Indian profile that’s clearly designed to appeal to a wider palate. However, the pricing does sit on the higher side for this category, which slightly affects the overall value equation.

I visited on a Monday around 3 PM and was seated in about 30 minutes—manageable by their standards. That said, this isn’t a place I’d personally queue up for on a busy weekend. It’s best experienced when the rush is relatively controlled.

If you’re in that part of the city, it’s definitely worth a visit once—more for the experience than as a regular go-to.

featured_reviews.name: Tarun Joseph
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Rameshwaram Cafe at Churchgate this morning for a quick breakfast like old times.
I’m a Kannadiga and I've lived in Bengaluru for a couple of years and used to visit Rameshwaram Cafe (Indiranagar and JP Nagar outlets), at least once a month. Even now, whenever I go back to Bengaluru, it’s a mandatory stop. So when they announced they were opening in Mumbai, I was genuinely excited. I’ve been missing proper dosa and idli here.

But what I ate today was not Rameshwaram Cafe.

I ordered my usual ghee pudi plain dosa and there was barely any pudi on it. The taste was completely off. It didn’t have the flavour, the texture, or even the smell that makes Rameshwaram Cafe what it is. The taste just felt different, very different. It honestly didn’t even feel like the Rameshwaram Cafe I remember from Bengaluru.
I didn’t try the pudi idli myself, but my friends ordered it and said it was just average as well.

After all the hype, the long queues, and the name they’ve built in Bengaluru, this was unbelievably disappointing. If this is what Rameshwaram Cafe Mumbai is serving, they’re just riding on the Bengaluru brand while delivering something far below that standard.

A truly mediocre experience. If you’ve actually eaten at the Bengaluru outlet, this will feel like a huge downgrade.

featured_reviews.name: Sachin Talwalkar
featured_reviews.review_text:

It was frequently patronized by the likes of Raj Kapoor, Dilip Kumar, and many cricketers. Recently renovated, you step into a regal experience - complete with uniformed waitstaff, European Art Deco accents, and live music.

The menu offers a unique mix of Indian dishes, a few European selections, and non-alcoholic beverages. Unique, because an ambience like this almost demands a glass of wine - something you sorely miss as piano renditions of old and new Bollywood compositions play on.

The food is excellent, the service could be better, but the experience is a must-have. One that transports you back to the charm of old Bombay.

featured_reviews.review_text:

Summer Breeze 4.5⭐

featured_reviews.review_text:
Earth Café, Churchgate feels like a quiet pause button in the middle of Mumbai’s relentless rhythm. Tucked away yet perfectly placed, this café welcomes you with an earthy charm that instantly soothes the senses. The moment you step in, you’re greeted by a calming blend of natural tones, soft lighting, and a thoughtfully curated space that feels both modern and grounded—true to its name.

The ambience strikes a beautiful balance between cozy and classy, making it ideal for everything from relaxed conversations to peaceful solo time. Whether you’re catching up with a friend, working on your laptop, or simply enjoying a slow meal, Earth Café creates an atmosphere that encourages you to linger a little longer.

The food is where the café truly shines. Every dish feels fresh, wholesome, and crafted with care. From vibrant salads and nourishing bowls to indulgent yet guilt-free desserts, the menu caters wonderfully to health-conscious diners without compromising on taste. The beverages—especially their coffees and refreshing coolers—are well-balanced and thoughtfully prepared, making them perfect companions to the food.

What stands out most is the attention to detail: warm service, beautifully plated dishes, and a sense of calm that’s rare in the heart of South Mumbai. Earth Café isn’t just a place to eat; it’s an experience—one that leaves you feeling lighter, happier, and eager to return.

A true gem at Churchgate, perfect for those who appreciate good food, serene vibes, and mindful living.

Cafe Bharat, Churchgate, is one of those old-school vegetarian cafés that quietly survives on routine rather than hype. No frills, no experiments, just straightforward food and a steady crowd of office-goers and regulars.

We had Puri Bhaji, Coffee, and Tikki Chole. The puri bhaji was simple and filling, nothing exceptional but nothing to complain about either. The bhaji was mildly spiced, homely in taste, and the puris were fresh enough. The tikki chole was decent; the tikkis were soft and the chole had a familiar North Indian flavour, though it didn’t stand out in any special way. The coffee was basic café-style, served hot, doing its job without trying to impress.

What works in Cafe Bharat’s favour is its budget-friendly pricing, quick service, and convenient location near Churchgate. It’s not a place you’d go out of your way to visit, but if you’re in the area and want a quick, affordable vegetarian meal, it does the job.

The ambience is functional and old-fashioned; clean, but clearly built for efficiency rather than comfort or aesthetics. Service is prompt and no-nonsense.

Overall, Cafe Bharat is reliable, modest, and predictable. Nothing great, nothing bad. Just a simple veg café that knows its role and sticks to it. Suitable for a quick bite, not for culinary excitement.

featured_reviews.name: Govind Sharma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Pizza By The Bay is truly one of Mumbai’s most iconic dining destinations, offering the perfect combination of great food, vibrant ambience, and an unbeatable sea-facing location on Marine Drive. The moment you step in, you’re welcomed by a lively, energetic vibe that instantly sets the mood for a memorable dining experience.
The biggest highlight is, without a doubt, the stunning view of the Arabian Sea. If you’re lucky enough to get a window-side seat, the experience becomes even more special—watching the waves while enjoying your meal is pure Mumbai magic. Whether it’s breakfast with the morning breeze, an evening meal with city lights, or a monsoon visit with rain and waves in the backdrop, the atmosphere here is always captivating.
The food quality is consistently good and flavorful. Their pizzas are perfectly baked with rich toppings and bold flavors, making them one of the best pizza spots in the city. Pasta, garlic bread, sandwiches, and breakfast options are equally satisfying. Both vegetarian and non-vegetarian dishes are well prepared, and the menu offers enough variety to suit different tastes, though a few items may feel premium-priced for the portions. Desserts and beverages like hot chocolate also stand out.
The ambience deserves special mention—antique-style décor, warm lighting, and a classy yet relaxed crowd give the place a timeless charm. It’s suitable for everything from solo visits and casual meet-ups to professional meetings and weekend outings. The place does get quite crowded, especially during peak hours and weekends, and waiting times can be long, but the experience is worth the patience.
Service is efficient and friendly, with staff guiding you well through the menu and attending promptly despite the crowd. While the lively atmosphere can make it a bit noisy, it adds to the overall energy of the place rather than taking away from it.
Overall, Pizza By The Bay is a must-visit for anyone who loves good food paired with a spectacular sea view. Slightly on the expensive side and often crowded, but the location, vibe, and quality make it a memorable 5-star experience. Perfect for creating beautiful Mumbai memories.

featured_reviews.name: sagar jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
This was my third visit to Santosham, and it continues to be a great spot for comforting, authentic South Indian food!
If you are looking for a complete traditional experience, their unlimited South Indian Thali is a must-try at least once. It’s a beautifully simple, home-style meal that tastes amazing. The thali comes fully loaded with a variety of authentic items—hot puris, steamed rice, flavorful and piping hot Sambar, a wonderfully tangy Rasam, and traditional sabjis like a dry Beans and Carrot Poriyal and a comforting Cabbage Kootu. They round it out with crisp appalams, fresh curd, pickle, and a sweet Payasam to finish it off. Just a quick heads-up: they have different pricing for the unlimited thali on weekdays versus weekends.
While the thali is fantastic and incredibly generous, it is quite a heavy meal. Personally, since we lean more toward classic South Indian snacks rather than massive authentic meals, the thali is a 'try it once for the experience' item for us.
If you aren't super hungry or just prefer lighter fare, absolutely go for their Idli and Dosa options instead. They are perfectly prepared and hit the spot every time. I also have to give a massive shoutout to their Dal Wada—it is incredibly crispy on the outside, perfectly spiced, and just flat-out delicious.

Staff is very helpful, one of the staff saw I m not adding Green chutney on rice, he came and suggested to use green chutney over the rice and it really tasted so good 😊
Overall verdict: Come hungry for the grand unlimited thali at least once, but you'll find yourself coming back regularly for the stellar dosas, idlis, and that amazing dal wada!

featured_reviews.name: Manikandan
featured_reviews.review_text: Santosham - Satvik South Indian Restaurant near Marine Drive is a clean and comforting spot for authentic South Indian vegetarian food in South Mumbai. The restaurant keeps a simple, traditional feel without trying to be overly fancy, and the food is the main highlight. Located in Marine Lines, it’s convenient after a walk along Marine Drive or nearby sightseeing. Service is quick, portions are satisfying, and the overall experience feels homely and consistent without being overpriced. One amazing thing is they serve meals and rice items throughout the day even at night.

featured_reviews.name: RACHNA TULI MASHKARIA
featured_reviews.review_text:
The banana leaf thali is not just a meal – it’s an experience that blends flavor, tradition, and hospitality in the most wholesome way. Served on a fresh banana leaf, the thali immediately brings a sense of authenticity and connection to Indian culinary roots.

What makes it truly special is the variety. From fragrant rice and comforting dals to vibrant curries, tangy pickles, crispy papad, and a sweet finish, every dish complements the other beautifully. The balance of flavors – spicy, tangy, salty, and sweet – ensures that every bite feels satisfying. The banana leaf itself adds a subtle earthy aroma while also being eco-friendly and hygienic.

Another highlight is the cultural warmth associated with it. The way servers lovingly add refills, encouraging you to eat to your heart’s content, makes the experience feel both generous and personal.

Overall, the banana leaf thali is not just good – it’s nourishing, soulful, and a celebration of food as tradition. Whether you’re a food enthusiast or someone who loves comfort meals, it’s definitely worth trying.

featured_reviews.name: Sarah Chamdawala
featured_reviews.review_text:
We had an amazing authentic South Indian breakfast at Santosham! Ordered the Mysore sada dosa, which was crispy and spicy and delicious; the ghee podi idli was fluffy and you could really taste the shuddh ghee; the beetroot rawa dosa was soo crispy and had just the perfect little hint of beetroot flavour; the benne dosa was yum and perfectly crispy on the outside and fluffy on the inside and served with the most decadent pure white butter! The filter coffees (both cold and hot) were also delicious with the perfect froth on top! We also enjoyed the rose milk with chia seeds. The tomato chutney, coconut chutney and sambhar served on the side were also great and proved the perfect accompaniments to the meal.
A special mention for the service which was top notch, thanks to Nasim and Uday who were very helpful and quick.
10/10 would recommend this place!

One of the best culinary experiences I’ve had in Mumbai. I stumbled upon this spot tucked into one of the city’s busiest, most crowded streets, and it was absolutely worth navigating the chaos to get there.

I ordered the pav bhaji and chole bhature, and both were outstanding. The pav bhaji was rich, buttery, and perfectly spiced with that authentic street-style flavor, yet it felt clean and hygienic. The chole bhature was just as impressive — fluffy, hot bhature paired with chole that had deep, balanced masala without being overly oily. You could taste the freshness in every bite.

What really elevated the experience was the staff. I was new to Mumbai and a bit overwhelmed, but they were incredibly friendly and patient. They took the time to explain the menu, recommend what to try, and even shared how each dish is traditionally eaten. At no point did I feel rushed despite the constant crowd outside.

I also noticed how neat and well-maintained the place was. For a busy street-side eatery, the tables were clean, the serving area was organized, and the staff did not feel rushed.

Great food, warm service, and surprising neatness in the heart of Mumbai’s bustle. I’ll definitely be back. Highly recommended if you want authentic flavors without compromising on hygiene
